newsitem.title: USA: SGS-Thomson sees lower Q3 gross margin.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson sees lower Q3 gross margin.

text.p: SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV, the French semiconductor manufacturer, said its gross margin this quarter could be below the 40.1 percent of last year's third quarter, a group vice president said, repeating a projection SGS-Thomson made in July.

Francois Guibert, group vice president, business development and investor relations, told the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference that SGS-Thomson also expects revenues to be below second quarter revenues of $1.05 billion but above year ago third quarter revenues of $922.6 million. SGS-Thomson stated also that projection in July.

Guilbert said the semiconductor industry worldwide is not as robust as it was a year ago, with pricing pressures on commodity products like memory products continuing. These are the reasons why margins may be under pressure, he said.
SGS-Thomson makes chips in both high growth areas like communications and smart card applications as well as more commodity type chips like memory.
The revenue dip from second quarter revenues is a seasonally normal trend that occurs many years but did not occur in 1995 because of the extraordinary strength of the semiconductor demand in 1995.
